newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU crude stocks fall, products rise in February.
newsitem.headline: EU crude stocks fall, products rise in February.

text.p: Crude oil stocks in the 14 countries of the European Union, excluding Sweden, fell sharply in February, while inventories of products rose, Stichting Euroilstocks said in its latest monthly report.

Crude and oil product stocks, as a whole, fell by 5.55 million barrels, or 0.5 percent, in February to 1,027 million barrels, but were still 22.55 million barrels, or 2.2 percent higher than in February 1996.
Crude oil stocks fell by 14.89 million barrels, or 3.7 percent, in February to 392.30 million barrels, leaving them 980,000 barrels, or 0.2 percent, lower than year-ago levels.
Middle distillate stocks rose by 7.13 million barrels, or 0.9 percent, to 302.63 million barrels, and were 28.74 million barrels, or 10.5 percent, higher than a year ago.
Gasoline inventories were up 1.45 million barrels, or 0.9 percent, in February to 166.05 million barrels, but were 7.21 million barrels, or 4.2 percent, lower than a year ago.
Fuel oil stocks were 2.08 million barrels, or 1.5 percent, higher at 141.38 million barrels. This left a year-on-year surplus of 3.75 million barrels, or 2.7 percent.
Naphtha stocks fell 1.32 million barrels to 24.64 million barrels.
Crude intake was 460,000 barrels per day (bpd) higher than in January at 11.982 million bpd, leading to a utilisation rate of 95.10 percent in February.
